asA: operator verifying a CLI or library release (rcf-lite itself)
iWant: the packed artefact installed as a brand-new consumer would install it
soThat: a release passes Verify only if it works with nothing borrowed from the developer's machine
title: The operator verifies a CLI or library against its packed artefact installed cold

acceptanceCriteria.description: [happy] Given a fixture package whose bound e2e test prints process.env.HOME, the npm cache path (npm config get cache run by the test) and whether a variable FIXTURE_LEAK set in the caller's environment is visible, when rcf verify run --release 1.1.0 --since v1.0.0 --package . --record runs, then the test observes a HOME and an npm cache inside the run's scratch directory under the OS temp directory, an empty cache before the install, and no FIXTURE_LEAK, and the report target reads kind "package", name, version, sha256 of the tarball and cold true.

[failure] Given --offline in release mode, the verb exits 2 with "[error] usage --offline cannot install cold"; given both --url and --artefact (or none of --url, --artefact and --package), it exits 2 with "[error] usage give exactly one target: --url, --artefact or --package"; given an artefact whose dependency resolves nowhere, it exits 1 naming the install command and writes no report.

[edge] Given a user npmrc at the caller's HOME that sets a registry the fixture cannot reach, when the cold release Verify runs, then the install ignores that npmrc and resolves from the default registry configuration, so a developer setting never changes the release result.

[must-not] A cold release Verify never writes in the project outside rcf/verify-reports/releases/ and rcf/fbs/ (and only with --record), never leaves a tarball, node_modules change or lockfile change in the project, and removes its scratch directory after the run.
